minutes.headline: Planning Board and Historical Commission worked over the Village Center District and the Architectural Preservation District drafts.
minutes.summary: At a joint session with the Historical Commission, the Planning Board held a second listening session on the draft Village Center District bylaw and reviewed the separate Architectural Preservation District (APD) draft. Topics were glazing percentages, first-floor residential limits, grandfathering of existing buildings, APD enforcement, and timing for the March 9 hearing and the March 23 warrant. A member's resignation was accepted, and a motion to ask the moderator for a tribute to a former planning director passed by voice vote.

public_comment.topic: Asked to be included as a joint meeting and argued for second-story requirement in the historic district.
A speaker raised concern that houses in the district becoming commercial would drive out residents and disagreed with the charette conclusions.
A speaker asked whether the historic preservation protections could be built into the village bylaw so they are not voted separately.

votes.motion: Write a letter to the town moderator asking that Town Meeting give a tribute to Marion Benson, former planning director.
Accept the resignation of Joanna Bellotta from the Planning Board.

budget_items.what_was_said: A speaker said holding a special town meeting to adopt APD design standards would incur a cost.
A speaker said the town's auctioned historic home sold at a very low price, illustrating the weak market for historic homes.

decisions.decision: Reuse provisions will apply to buildings existing as of a fixed date (around May 1, 2015) rather than 'existing' at any time.
Board consensus to set the minimum glazing percentage around 35 percent for campus development.
Board leaned toward exempting existing residential uses from the 25 percent first-floor residential cap in mixed use.
Adam to work with the Historical Commission on APD revisions ahead of the March 9 and March 23 deadlines.
Delay of VCD effectiveness until the APD rules exist to be investigated and brought to the March 9 meeting.
Proposal for seven members and four meetings a month to be put on the March 9 agenda.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board and Historical Commission met jointly on the draft Village Center District bylaw and the separate Architectural Preservation District draft.
The board reached consensus on a minimum glazing percentage for campus development and leaned toward exempting existing residential uses from the first-floor residential cap.
Adam is to work with the Historical Commission on Architectural Preservation District revisions ahead of the March 9 and March 23 deadlines.
Whether to delay the Village Center District taking effect until the preservation rules exist is to be investigated and brought to March 9.
A motion to ask the town moderator for a Town Meeting tribute to a former planning director passed; the vote on a member's resignation was not audible.

why_it_matters: The Village Center District rules on ground-floor housing, storefront glass and existing buildings will shape what can be built or converted in the village centre, and residents will be asked to vote on them at Town Meeting.
If the preservation district needs its own vote, that could mean a separate or special town meeting, which the minutes say would carry a cost.
watch_next: March 9 Planning Board meeting: the hearing, the finding on delaying the Village Center District, and a proposal for seven members and four meetings a month.
March 23 warrant deadline for the Village Center District and Architectural Preservation District articles.
